title: Customer portal database connection pool exhaustion
description: The Customer portal (site_id 1002) is intermittently returning HTTP 500 responses during periods of elevated traffic. Application logs show repeated connection acquisition timeouts from the PostgreSQL connection pool, followed by successful requests once existing connections are released. The database remains reachable and accepts direct connections, but the application frequently reaches its configured connection limit. The issue is concentrated on requests that load customer account history, where several database queries remain active for significantly longer than normal. Investigation should compare active database sessions against application pool metrics, identify queries holding connections for extended periods, and determine whether slow queries, connection leaks, or insufficient pool sizing are contributing to the exhaustion. Restarting affected application instances provides temporary relief, but the underlying connection usage should be investigated before simply increasing the pool size.

title: Online store intermittently returning 502 errors
description: The Online store (site_id 1005) is intermittently returning HTTP 502 responses from the reverse proxy when customers access product and checkout endpoints. The upstream application processes remain running and continue passing basic health checks, but the proxy logs contain upstream connection reset and timeout messages. The failures are more frequent for requests that perform database-backed operations and appear to correlate with periods of increased request latency. The issue does not consistently affect the same application instance, suggesting that the problem may involve a shared dependency or proxy timeout rather than a single unhealthy server. Investigation should correlate reverse-proxy timing information with application request logs, database latency, and upstream connection counts. A temporary workaround is to increase the relevant proxy timeout if necessary while monitoring connection accumulation and investigating the underlying application latency.

title: Developer documentation deployment pods repeatedly restarting
description: The Developer documentation (site_id 1004) is repeatedly restarting after the latest application rollout. New containers start successfully and initially respond to health checks, but terminate between 30 and 90 seconds later. Container logs indicate a failure while initializing the Redis-backed documentation search cache. Redis itself is reachable from other workloads in the environment, suggesting that the problem may be specific to configuration injected into the new deployment. The previous application version continues operating normally. The deployment introduced a new cache configuration variable, and the failing containers report a parsing error when that value is missing or malformed. Investigation should compare the effective environment variables and Secret references between the previous and current deployment versions. Rolling back to the previous version is a suitable workaround while the new configuration is validated.

title: Partner extranet event processing backlog
description: The Partner extranet (site_id 1003) has developed a steadily increasing backlog of asynchronous partner-update events. Events continue to arrive at approximately the expected rate, but the worker service is processing them substantially slower than normal. Consumer CPU utilization is moderate while database write latency has increased significantly. Worker logs show repeated transaction retries when persisting partner status changes, followed by successful commits after several attempts. No queue broker outage or partition reassignment issue has been detected. If the backlog continues to grow, partner-facing information may become increasingly stale. Investigation should examine database locks, slow write queries, transaction retry frequency, and worker processing time before increasing worker concurrency. Additional workers may provide temporary relief if the queue supports parallel processing, but database contention should be addressed before scaling consumers indefinitely.

title: Internal HR portal authentication failures after key rotation
description: The Internal HR portal (site_id 1007) is intermittently returning invalid-session errors when users navigate between authenticated pages. The authentication service successfully issues tokens, but some HR portal instances reject newly generated tokens because the signing key identifier is not present in their locally cached verification key set. The problem started shortly after an automated authentication-key rotation. Different application instances appear to have reloaded their configuration at different times, so requests can succeed or fail depending on which instance receives the request. Investigation should compare the active signing and verification key identifiers across the authentication service and all HR portal instances and verify how configuration changes are propagated. A temporary workaround is to keep the previous verification key available to all consumers while synchronizing the new configuration, followed by a controlled reload of affected instances.

title: Corporate website large file uploads failing
description: The Corporate website (site_id 1001) accepts small file uploads normally but consistently fails when users submit files larger than approximately 50 MB. The application returns a generic upload error after several minutes, while server logs indicate that the multipart upload session is terminated before the final parts are transferred. Connectivity to the storage backend is stable and smaller multipart uploads complete successfully. The failure threshold appears to correspond with the configured request body limit and reverse-proxy timeout rather than a storage-provider outage. Investigation should check upload-size and timeout settings at the CDN, reverse proxy, web application, and storage-client layers. It should also be determined whether large files are streamed or buffered in application memory. As a temporary workaround, users can split large uploads into smaller files while the request limits and timeout configuration are reviewed.

title: Payroll system backups missing audit tables
description: The Payroll system (site_id 1008) reports successful completion of its nightly database backup, but recent restore testing shows that several large audit tables are absent from the generated backup archive. The export command exits successfully and the resulting archive can be opened, but its table list differs from previous known-good backups. The missing tables are not consistently the same, suggesting that schema discovery or an exclusion rule may be dependent on database permissions or generated configuration. The live Payroll system remains operational and no production data loss has been observed. Investigation should compare the database role used by the backup job, the exact generated export command, the discovered schema and table list, and the contents of the resulting archive. Until the issue is resolved, the existing automated backup should not be considered sufficient for disaster recovery. An independently verified full database export should be retained as a temporary safeguard.

title: Legacy intranet DNS resolution failures
description: The Legacy intranet (site_id 1012) is intermittently unable to resolve internal hostnames required by several application functions. Browser requests occasionally fail with DNS resolution errors and then succeed after a retry. The issue is not isolated to a single workstation and has been reproduced from multiple internal network segments. DNS resolver logs show elevated query volume and an increase in timeout responses during the affected periods. The Legacy intranet also performs several DNS lookups for backend services during each page request, which may amplify the problem when resolver performance degrades. Investigation should examine resolver CPU and memory usage, query volume, cache effectiveness, upstream DNS latency, and recent changes to the intranet's service-discovery configuration. Reducing unnecessary DNS lookups and temporarily increasing resolver capacity may reduce the frequency of failures while the root cause is investigated.

title: Support knowledge base incorrectly rate limiting users
description: The Support knowledge base (site_id 1010) is returning HTTP 429 responses to legitimate users even though their individual request rates remain below the documented limits. The issue is particularly common for users accessing the knowledge base through corporate NAT gateways, where multiple users share the same public source IP address. The current rate-limiting middleware combines source IP and session identity for certain endpoints, causing requests from unrelated users to consume the same throttling bucket. Logs show that individual sessions remain within their expected limits while the shared IP bucket reaches its threshold. Investigation should reproduce the behavior from multiple clients sharing one public address and inspect how the throttling key is generated for affected routes. Increasing the shared-IP threshold can provide temporary relief, but the preferred fix is to ensure that independent users are not incorrectly sharing the same quota bucket.

title: Marketing landing page serving stale campaign content
description: The Marketing landing page (site_id 1011) continues serving an older version of campaign content several minutes after the publishing process reports a successful update. The origin server contains the new content and direct requests that bypass the CDN return the expected version, but normal visitor traffic continues receiving cached responses from edge locations. Cache invalidation logs show that the publishing workflow completed without reporting an error, yet the corresponding cache keys remain present at multiple edge locations. The issue appears limited to content published through the automated campaign workflow; manual cache purges update the page immediately. Investigation should compare cache-key generation between automated publishing and manual purge operations and verify that the invalidation request targets all relevant CDN paths. A temporary workaround is to manually purge the affected paths after each campaign publication until automated invalidation is corrected.

title: Careers page showing stale job listings
description: The Careers page (site_id 1006) reads job listings from a read replica that is currently several minutes behind the primary database. New or recently modified job postings appear correctly when queried against the primary database but remain absent from the public Careers page until replication catches up. Monitoring shows that WAL generation on the primary has increased while replay throughput on the replica has remained relatively stable. The replica is also handling several expensive reporting queries that consume disk I/O and compete with replication replay. Investigation should compare replication lag against WAL generation rate, replay throughput, disk utilization, and long-running queries on the replica. A temporary workaround is to route time-sensitive job-listing reads to the primary database or reduce nonessential queries running on the replica until replication returns to normal.

title: Customer portal TLS handshake failures for legacy clients
description: The Customer portal (site_id 1002) is inaccessible to a subset of users on older managed devices following a recent load balancer security-policy update. Modern browsers and current operating systems connect normally, while affected clients fail during the TLS handshake before an HTTP request reaches the application. Load balancer logs indicate that the affected clients offer older TLS versions or cipher suites that are no longer accepted by the active policy. There has been no corresponding change to the Customer portal application itself. Investigation should identify the TLS protocol and cipher combinations presented by affected clients and compare them with the current load balancer policy. The preferred remediation is to update affected client software, but if immediate compatibility is required, a separately scoped legacy endpoint can be considered without weakening the primary portal's security configuration.

title: Online store product cache not being invalidated
description: The Online store (site_id 1005) continues displaying outdated product prices and stock availability after administrators modify products in the back-office system. Direct database queries show that the new values are committed immediately, but the public API continues returning the previous values until the associated cache entries expire naturally. Bulk catalog imports correctly invalidate cache entries, while individual administrative updates do not. Application traces show that the administrative update transaction completes successfully but no cache-invalidation event is emitted afterward. This creates a risk that customers may see an old price or purchase an item that has already become unavailable. Investigation should compare the event flow between bulk imports and individual updates and verify whether the expected invalidation event is generated, delivered, and processed. A temporary workaround is to manually purge the affected product cache keys after administrative changes.

title: Partner extranet duplicate synchronization jobs
description: The Partner extranet (site_id 1003) is occasionally processing the same partner synchronization job more than once. Duplicate executions have resulted in repeated outbound update requests for a small number of partners. The queue uses at-least-once delivery, but the worker performs the external operation before recording the job as completed. When processing exceeds the queue visibility timeout, the original message becomes visible to another worker even though the first worker is still active. Logs show overlapping executions for the same job identifier. Investigation should compare the configured visibility timeout with the maximum expected processing duration and determine whether the external partner operation supports idempotency keys. A temporary mitigation is to increase the visibility timeout and introduce worker-side duplicate detection, while ensuring that failed jobs can still be retried safely.

title: Internal HR portal memory usage continuously increasing
description: The Internal HR portal (site_id 1007) application instances gradually consume more memory after processing employee-report requests and do not return to their normal baseline after the requests finish. Instances initially operate within expected memory limits, but resident memory grows continuously until containers approach their configured memory limit and are restarted by the runtime. The problem is significantly more pronounced for reports containing large employee datasets or generated documents. Preliminary profiling suggests that generated report objects or cached employee data remain referenced after the request completes. Restarting an affected instance restores normal memory usage temporarily, but the problem reappears as additional reports are generated. Investigation should capture heap profiles before and after large report operations and identify retained objects or unbounded caches. A temporary workaround is to limit report size and concurrency and recycle affected application instances on a controlled schedule.

title: Status page monitoring data delayed
description: The Status page (site_id 1009) is displaying infrastructure health information with a delay of approximately 10 to 15 minutes. Individual monitoring agents continue generating metrics normally, but the central ingestion pipeline is processing them significantly slower than usual. The ingestion queue has accumulated a growing backlog while collector nodes show elevated CPU utilization and increased network traffic. No permanent data loss has been confirmed, but the delayed metrics mean that incidents may not appear on the Status page until well after they begin. Investigation should determine whether the increased processing time is caused by higher metric volume, collector saturation, network throughput, or reduced backend ingestion capacity. A temporary mitigation could involve reducing high-cardinality or nonessential metrics and increasing collector capacity so that critical service-health metrics can be processed first.

title: Developer documentation search returning incomplete results
description: The Developer documentation (site_id 1004) is returning incomplete results for recently published API reference pages. The new pages are visible when accessed directly by URL, but they do not appear in search results until several hours later. Older documentation continues to be indexed correctly. Indexing-worker logs show that the documentation publication event is generated successfully, but some indexing jobs fail while retrieving newly generated pages because the renderer has not yet completed the associated asset generation. The failed indexing jobs are marked as completed instead of being retried, leaving the search index permanently behind until a full reindex is triggered. Investigation should correlate publication events with renderer completion times and inspect the failure handling of indexing jobs. A temporary workaround is to run a targeted reindex for newly published documentation after deployment while correcting the event ordering and retry behavior.

title: Payroll system configuration inconsistent across instances
description: The Payroll system (site_id 1008) is exhibiting inconsistent timeout behavior when communicating with an external payroll provider. Approximately one third of production instances continue using the previous 30-second provider timeout, while the remaining instances use the newly configured 90-second value. Requests routed to the older instances fail when the provider responds slowly, whereas the same requests succeed when handled by instances with the updated configuration. The deployment controller reports all instances as healthy because the configuration is loaded only during application startup and the deployment did not restart containers whose image digest remained unchanged. Investigation should compare the effective runtime configuration on every Payroll system instance against the desired configuration and verify how configuration changes are propagated. A controlled restart of all affected instances can be used as an immediate workaround, followed by verification that every instance reports the same effective timeout before normal traffic is restored.
